data.title: Romania to receive C-130H Hercules aircraft from the US
data.description: Romania will receive a C-130H Hercules aircraft from the United States government on Wednesday, October 14, the Defense Ministry (MApN) announced, as reported by News.ro . A handover ceremony will take place at the Romanian Air Force’s 90th Airlift Base in Otopeni. Defense minister Radu Miruță and US ambassador to Romania Darryl Nirenberg are expected to attend the event. The aircraft is being transferred free of charge through the Excess Defense Articles (EDA) program, which allows eligible countries to receive surplus US military equipment, the ministry explained. “Romania has benefited from the EDA program since 1996, when C-130B aircraft were integrated into the Romanian Air Force’s transport fleet. This is the eighth aircraft of this type to enter service with the Romanian Armed Forces through the EDA program,” reads the MApN statement . The C-130H can conduct air transport, medical evacuation, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief missions. The ministry said the transfer also highlights the defense cooperation developed during nearly three decades of strategic partnership between Romania and the United States.

data.title: Romania’s Forestry Guard launches digital platform for complaints
data.description: The National Forestry Guard launched a new digital platform on Monday, October 12, through which citizens can submit and track complaints regarding illegal tree cutting and other irregularities in forests, as well as consult a map showing the locations of inspections carried out by inspectors, the damage identified, and the penalties imposed. The new application, presented by interim environment minister Diana Buzoianu and National Forestry Guard general inspector Florin George Gârbacea at a press conference, aims both to increase the transparency of inspections and to change the way complaints regarding violations of forestry legislation are registered, resolved, and evaluated. The application includes information on the historical boundaries of forest land, dating back to 1990, data from forestry management plans, and a system for evaluating the performance of the nine regional forestry guards. It was developed within the institution, without contracting external programming services. The minister explained that, until now, citizens submitting petitions regarding possible illegal tree cutting had no tool available to track what happened to their complaints. Inspections could take months, and petitioners had to wait for the institution’s response without being able to access information about the progress of the inspection or its results. Through the new platform, each complaint submitted online will automatically receive a registration number, which will be sent to the petitioner by email. They will subsequently be able to check the status of the petition, the time elapsed since registration, whether an inspection has been carried out, and the conclusions of the checks. The system includes a timeline of the complaint resolution process, from registration to the communication of the response. https://www.facebook.com/DianaBuzoianu/videos/968539316296158/ Moreover, the electronic form allows for documents that can help inspectors identify the location and nature of the reported irregularities to be attached. Citizens are encouraged to submit photographs with GPS location data, geographical coordinates, cadastral documents, and other relevant materials. Gârbacea explained that this information can be particularly important when unmarked tree stumps, suspicious tree cutting, or interventions in areas where the boundaries of forest land are unclear are reported. The application also tracks compliance with deadlines for resolving petitions. The general inspector stated that after a complaint is registered, the system automatically calculates the 30-day response deadline. In the internal module, petitions that are still within the deadline are marked in green, while those that have exceeded it are highlighted in red. Depending on the complexity of the inspections, the deadline may also be extended in accordance with the law. The platform includes an interactive map displaying Forestry Guard inspections and their geographical locations. Users can select an inspection to view a summary of the checks and a report containing their results, including whether violations of the law were identified and whether fines were imposed. Public information within the form is anonymized, meaning that the names of people who filed complaints will not be displayed, and inspection reports will not include identifying information about the companies inspected. According to the general inspector, this measure is important because some citizens hesitate to report irregularities for fear that their identities might become known. The platform is not limited to inspections initiated following complaints. According to the Forestry Guard’s leadership, all inspections carried out by inspectors will eventually be entered into the system, regardless of whether they were prompted by citizens’ petitions or initiated by the institution itself. At the time of the launch, however, not all inspections had been uploaded to the application. During the demonstration, Gârbacea explained that more inspections had been carried out than were visible on the map, and that some features, including those for mobile phone use, were still under development. The environment minister stated that people who have filed complaints can request to participate in inspections carried out by forestry inspectors. The measure was not introduced through the new platform but through a decision by the general inspector that had already been in effect for several weeks. Buzoianu explained that there had been complaints that inspectors arriving at a site did not check the exact locations indicated in the reports. According to her, the presence of petitioners can help identify the exact locations where possible illegal activities have been observed and prevent situations in which inspections are carried out in an area other than the one reported. The environment minister also presented data on the Forestry Guard’s activity during the first six months of 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. In this period, the number of inspections increased by approximately 9–10%, while the value of the damage identified reached RON 3.85 million, compared with RON 1.34 million in the first half of last year. Buzoianu stated that these results were achieved with the same number of inspectors and the same inspection tools, noting that the difference was related to the prioritization of checks and changes in the leadership of some regional units. The volume of illegally cut timber identified by inspectors also increased, from approximately 2,700–2,800 cubic meters in the first six months of 2025 to around 6,000 cubic meters in the same period of 2026.

During the demonstration, Gârbacea explained that more inspections had been carried out than were visible on the map, and that some features, including those for mobile phone use, were still under development. The environment minister stated that people who have filed complaints can request to participate in inspections carried out by forestry inspectors. The measure was not introduced through the new platform but through a decision by the general inspector that had already been in effect for several weeks. Buzoianu explained that there had been complaints that inspectors arriving at a site did not check the exact locations indicated in the reports. According to her, the presence of petitioners can help identify the exact locations where possible illegal activities have been observed and prevent situations in which inspections are carried out in an area other than the one reported. The environment minister also presented data on the Forestry Guard’s activity during the first six months of 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. In this period, the number of inspections increased by approximately 9–10%, while the value of the damage identified reached RON 3.85 million, compared with RON 1.34 million in the first half of last year. Buzoianu stated that these results were achieved with the same number of inspectors and the same inspection tools, noting that the difference was related to the prioritization of checks and changes in the leadership of some regional units. The volume of illegally cut timber identified by inspectors also increased, from approximately 2,700–2,800 cubic meters in the first six months of 2025 to around 6,000 cubic meters in the same period of 2026.

data.title: Romania’s Electric Castle announces dates for 2027 edition
data.description: The 13th edition of Romania’s Electric Castle festival will take place from July 15 to 18, 2027, organizers announced. Hundreds of artists and activities are expected, with the lineup to be announced at a later date. General-access passes are already on sale, with prices starting at EUR 159 plus fees. “On the program: something new - hundreds of artists and experiences; something old - a centuries-old castle with stories waiting to be continued; and something blue - the July sky, with spectacular sunsets competing with the main-stage shows,” organizers said, as quoted by News.ro . The 2026 edition of Electric Castle attracted 272,000 attendees. More than 20 full concerts from this year’s festival are also being released on its YouTube channel, including performances by Teddy Swims, Archive, Dub Pistols, Kneecap, and House of Protection. Details about the 2027 edition and tickets are available on the event’s website.

data.title: Swiss manufacturer VAT expands factory in Romania’s Arad
data.description: VAT Romania, a subsidiary of Switzerland-based VAT Group, announced that it is expanding its factory in Arad by approximately 800 sqm, just over a year after the production facility opened. The expansion is intended to support a gradual shift from components and subassemblies to finished products shipped directly to customers. The construction is scheduled for completion by mid-December 2026. The additional space will include a shipping area for finished products, more storage capacity, and facilities supporting final assembly. The component production capacity at the Arad plant increased by approximately 30% in 2026, with another expansion planned for 2027. VAT is also investing in local final-product assembly, automation, and digitalization. “The development of the Arad factory confirms the potential we identified in Romania when we decided to build the new production facility,” said Alin Crețu, general manager of VAT Romania. “Demand from the semiconductor industry and the capabilities we have developed here allow us to continue this evolution and gradually introduce new products and production processes in Arad.” The factory currently produces components and products for the semiconductor, display, and photovoltaic industries, as well as scientific instruments and particle accelerator applications. The production involves high-precision machining processes such as milling and turning. The resulting components are used in systems where precision, purity, and airtightness are required for vacuum-based manufacturing, the company said. “Romania has strengthened its important role in our global production network, supplying components and assemblies used in some of the world’s most advanced technologies,” VAT Group CEO Urs Gantner stated. The Romanian subsidiary had more than 500 employees at the end of the first half of 2026, an increase of over 50% from the end of 2025. The number of employees directly involved in production rose by more than 70% over the same period, and the company expects further workforce growth in 2027. All products manufactured at the Arad plant are exported, currently to European markets. VAT has operated in Romania since 2001, initially through a company called SYSMEC, which was fully integrated into VAT Group in 2008 and renamed VAT Romania in 2019. Arad is now one of the group’s three main operational centers worldwide, alongside facilities in Switzerland and Malaysia. The factory opened in June 2025 and includes more than 3,000 sqm of cleanroom production space. VAT Group, which specializes in high-performance vacuum valves, reported net sales of CHF 1.07 billion in 2025 and employs nearly 4,000 people worldwide.

data.title: IMF forecasts 0.5% recession in Romania in 2026, slower recovery in 2027
data.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) sharply revised its estimates for Romania’s economy this month, forecasting a recession this year and a slower recovery in 2027 than initially expected, according to data analyzed by Profit.ro . Romania’s economy is now expected to shrink by 0.5% in 2026, compared with growth of 0.7% estimated in the spring. The new estimate is in line with that of the World Bank , which was also recently revised downward. At the same time, the IMF anticipated economic growth of 2.2% in 2027 for Romania, compared with the previously estimated 2.5% increase. The current account deficit is similarly expected to widen to 7% of GDP in 2026, up 0.2% from the previous forecast, and narrow to 6.7% of GDP next year. Labor market conditions are also expected to deteriorate, with the unemployment rate forecast to rise to 6.5% this year, compared with 6.1% in 2025 and the previously projected rate of 6% forecast by the IMF. Globally, the IMF has kept its forecast for growth of 3.1% in 2026 unchanged, noting the positive demand-side effect of investments in artificial intelligence and related infrastructure and hardware equipment. Global economic growth is expected to accelerate to 3.4% in 2027, very close to the 3.5% increase recorded last year. However, the IMF warns that the apparent stability of the global economy actually masks a redistribution of growth among countries, depending on their exposure to the supply shock caused by wars and the intensity of demand associated with artificial intelligence. “Currently, 32 economies generate 95% of global growth, compared with 54 economies in April, while downward revisions have become more frequent, affecting approximately 47% of economies,” according to the report . Geopolitical risks, particularly in the Middle East, will continue to impact trade relations and economic activity, according to the IMF. The negative supply shock generated by the war is spreading through the economy via higher and more volatile energy prices, as well as their impact on inflation dynamics. “So far, the private sector appears to have adapted well to the geopolitical shocks caused by direct conflicts and trade disputes. However, as short periods of calm alternate with waves of attacks in a prolonged and protracted conflict, some of the adjustment mechanisms that protected the global economy in the initial phase — based on the assumption that hostilities would be short-lived — are narrowing, and the risk of higher economic costs is becoming increasingly evident,” the report also stated.

data.title: Record attendance at anniversary edition of Spotlight Festival in Bucharest
data.description: More than 320,000 people attended the tenth edition of Spotlight – International Light Festival, held between October 9 and 11, 2026, in downtown Bucharest. During the event, building façades became surfaces for video mapping shows, while urban spaces hosted immersive installations and light sculptures. PLAYGROUND, the theme of the anniversary edition, proposed a playful relationship between people, light, and urban space. This year’s edition also involved a major technical and logistical operation. Preparing the festival required seven days of installation work, the involvement of 20 technicians, the installation of more than three kilometers of cables and optical fiber, the use of 20 laser video projectors, and more than 200 light sources. The Spotlight experience extended beyond the festival’s main route through installations presented at Promenada Mall, Mega Mall, and ARCUB – Hanul Gabroveni. The anniversary edition of Spotlight also had an important international dimension. For the first time, Bucharest hosted the annual meeting of the International Light Festivals Organisation (ILO), an organization bringing together light festivals and professionals in the field from around the world. The event brought directors and representatives of international festivals, artists, and light art specialists to ARCUB – Hanul Gabroveni, strengthening Bucharest’s role in the international dialogue on art, technology, and the creative use of public space. At the same time, the second edition of Spotlight Talks, held on October 10 and 11 under the theme “Light, Art & the City,” gave the public access to presentations, debates, and meetings with artists and professionals in the field of light art. The program included discussions on the role of light festivals in transforming cities, the relationship between art and the public, women’s perspectives in light art, and the creative processes behind multimedia projects. Artists and studios from Romania, France, and the United Kingdom presented projects and artistic approaches in an open dialogue with the public and the local creative community. The anniversary edition also marked the end of the 2026 season of the “Străzi Deschise – București” (“Open Streets – Bucharest”) project, with both events contributing to transforming Calea Victoriei into a space dedicated to culture, social interaction, and urban exploration.

data.title: Three Romanian workers drown in water tank in southern Portugal
data.description: Three Romanian workers, aged 21, 24, and 40, drowned while carrying out waterproofing work inside a water tank in Quinta do Lago, a locality in southern Portugal. Aside from the Romanians, three other people received medical attention at the scene. According to Portuguese publication Notícias ao Minuto , the victims were found dead in the water tank of a private property. The information was confirmed by the National Republican Guard and the District Command for Relief Operations. The exact cause of the accident has not yet been established. The local labor inspectorate is set to investigate the circumstances in which the tragedy occurred.

data.title: Metropolis Foundation’s Bucharest pediatric psychiatry clinic needs EUR 9.5 mln for completion
data.description: Construction of what is expected to become Romania’s largest pediatric psychiatry clinic has reached the building’s fourth and final floor, according to the Metropolis Foundation. The organization has raised EUR 7 million of the EUR 16.5 million required for the project and says at least EUR 9.5 million is still needed. Work on the new clinic at the Prof. Dr. Alexandru Obregia Psychiatry Hospital began on October 10, 2025, World Mental Health Day. The building will have a usable area of approximately 4,000 sqm, including a basement, ground floor, and four upper floors. Crews are currently completing the slab above the fourth floor and continuing masonry work. The next stages include enclosing the building, installing utility systems, dividing the interior, and fitting out its medical, therapeutic, and rehabilitation spaces, the foundation said. The clinic will include patient rooms adapted for children, medical offices, occupational therapy rooms, sensory spaces, virtual reality therapy facilities, and educational areas. A specialized unit will also treat adolescents facing addiction. “One year ago, we were standing on a plot where we planned to build a hospital. Today, the building has reached its top floor, thanks to the people and companies that believed in our mission,” said Codin Maticiuc, president of the Metropolis Foundation. “We still have a long and costly road ahead before the first child can be treated here. We have shown that we can build a hospital with private funds. Now we need the same mobilization to complete it.” The foundation said demand for pediatric mental health care at Obregia Hospital has increased significantly. The number of children and adolescents treated there rose from 4,424 in 2019 to 5,711 in 2025, while the share of severe cases increased from 57% to 79%. Over the same period, recorded cases of depression increased almost fivefold, anxiety cases more than sevenfold, and suicide attempts from 9 to 489, according to the same source. The project is being developed through the foundation’s Public Hospitals from Private Funds initiative in partnership with Bucharest City Hall, the Bucharest Hospitals and Medical Services Administration, and Obregia Hospital. The foundation is inviting companies and individuals to support the project, with donation details available here .

data.title: DP World launches EUR 53.8 mln electrification project at Constanța Port terminal
data.description: DP World announced that it launched a EUR 53.8 million project to electrify its container terminal at the Port of Constanța in Romania. The investment, co-financed by the European Union, is scheduled for completion by August 31, 2028. The financing package includes an EU grant of up to EUR 19.7 million through the Connecting Europe Facility, a loan of up to EUR 25 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, and a contribution from terminal operator Constanța South Container Terminal. The project will electrify 29 container blocks through the installation of approximately 6 km of busbar infrastructure designed to power electric rubber-tired gantry cranes. DP World will also build a charging hub with 10 charging points and acquire 10 electric terminal tractors. A dedicated transformer station will support the new vehicles. Two onshore power supply systems, also known as cold ironing systems, will allow docked vessels to connect to shore-side electricity rather than operate their auxiliary engines while in port. The systems will be powered exclusively by electricity from renewable sources, the company said. The investment also includes three transformer stations, each fitted with three 2,000 kVA transformers, as well as two 5 MVA transformers for the shore-power systems. The project is part of a wider electrification program that includes a separate EUR 46.2 million investment in remotely operated electric gantry cranes, two electric mobile harbor cranes, and additional electric terminal tractors. The two components will bring DP World’s total planned investment in electrifying its Constanța operations to EUR 100 million. Romania’s Port of Constanța is the largest port on the Black Sea and an important hub on the EU’s Trans-European Transport Network. Constanța South Container Terminal operates under DP World, a global logistics and port terminal company headquartered in Dubai.

data.title: Romania’s annual inflation rises to 6.6% in September as fuel prices surge
data.description: Romania's annual inflation rate in September 2026, compared with September 2025, was 6.6%, the National Institute of Statistics reported on Tuesday, October 13. In August, the annual inflation rate was 6.2%. The INS noted that after three months of deflation, annual inflation resumed its upward trend in September 2026. Overall, the annual inflation rate, compared with the same month of the previous year, was 6.61%, with the largest price increases once again recorded in services, at 11.12%. Over the same period, non-food goods prices rose 7.06%, while food prices rose 3%. “The average rate of change in consumer prices over the last 12 months (October 2025 – September 2026) compared with the previous 12 months (October 2024 – September 2025) was 9.2%,” the INS stated in a press release. Among food products, the largest price increases over this period were once again recorded for coffee, whose price rose by 13.78% in one year. Eggs ranked second, with a price increase of 10.84%, while edible oil became 7.62% more expensive. Cow’s milk increased in price by 7.56% over the same period. For meat, prices rose by 8.5% for beef and 3.34% for both pork and poultry. Fresh fish increased in price by 5.44%, while the category of canned fish rose by 5.33%. Sugar and honey products saw prices increase by 5.81% compared with September 2025, while sugar itself fell in price by 1.67%. Among alcoholic beverages, țuică and other spirits became 5.01% more expensive, while wine rose by 4.15% and beer by 4.9%. Other food price increases were recorded for bread, up 4.79%; cow’s milk telemea cheese, up 3.75%; and sheep’s milk telemea cheese, up 3.0%. Price decreases in September 2026 compared with the same period of the previous year were recorded for butter, down 0.96%; flour, down 3.23%; and cornmeal, down 3.42%. Annual price decreases were also recorded for potatoes, down 3.64%, and fresh fruit, down 16.69%. Among non-food goods, the most significant increases in September were recorded for diesel, up 37.61%, followed by gasoline, up 28.42%. Electricity, which until recently had been the leading contributor to annual price increases, rose by only 1.35% following the end of the base effect resulting from the removal of the price cap support scheme. Other price increases in this category were recorded for thermal energy (10.70%), knitwear (7.0%), books, newspapers, and magazines (6.36%), detergents (6.25%), and tobacco and cigarettes (5.72%). Last but not least, hygiene products and cosmetics became 4.41% more expensive, while medicine prices rose by 1.9% in September. Between September 2025 and September 2026, gas prices increased by 4.63%. One category that has received little attention so far, watches, video equipment, and sporting goods, saw prices rise by 8.53% over one year. The INS noted that, within the services category, the largest price increases in September 2026 compared with the same month in 2025 were recorded for rents, which rose by 39.46%, followed by water, sewerage, and sanitation services, up 14.11%, and television subscriptions, up 14.02%. Other significant annual increases in this category were recorded for car repairs (8.89%), hygiene and cosmetic services (8.12%), and clothing and footwear manufacturing and repair services (8.40%). Meanwhile, medical care became 8.53% more expensive, urban transport fares increased by 2.46%, and road transport fares rose by 8.58%. Car subscription fees increased by 9.77%, while air transport service prices rose by 1.32% compared with September of the previous year. However, in this case, prices fell by 14% compared with August 2026. Postal service rates in September 2026 increased by 9.32% compared with the same month in 2025, restaurant and café services became 6.14% more expensive over one year, and hotel room prices rose by 3.47%.

data.title: IAR Brașov employees protest as board remuneration rises more than fourfold
data.description: Last week, interim economy minister Irineu Darău announced that the state had increased the gross monthly allowances of IAR Brașov board members from RON 4,720 to RON 20,400. The state should support performance based on objective indicators rather than proximity to a particular minister or political party, he argued. Darău said he had established a formula for calculating board members’ remuneration that takes into account the company’s size, turnover, number of employees, profitability, investments, listed-company status and the complexity of the mandate. “Yesterday [Tuesday], I signed the mandate stating that at IAR Brașov the Romanian state, as a responsible shareholder, should support performance based on objective indicators, not on proximity to one minister or another, one party or another. Expectations are high, and I have made them clear to the members of the Board of Directors and the executive management,” the interim minister said. According to Darău, the Brașov-based company has a long-standing industrial cooperation with Airbus Helicopters, including in helicopter production, customisation and maintenance.

data.title: Romania’s PM-designate sketches technocratic government but seeks political backing
data.description: Despite proposing the six-month truce, Luca Niculescu has publicly said he wants the government to remain in office for two years, until the 2028 elections, Digi24 reported. Niculescu has reportedly sketched a technocratic cabinet but still hopes to secure the involvement of political parties. The Social Democrats (PSD), however, have so far refused to support such a government, according to party leader Sorin Grindeanu, who spoke at a press conference on October 12. The two main parties capable of assembling a parliamentary majority with their partners, the PSD and the Liberals (PNL), remain at odds. The PSD abandoned the governing coalition in April after breaking with the common governing strategy, but is now seeking to restore the arrangement. The Social Democrats insist on bringing the PNL, or at least part of it, back into government - but on their ruling strategy. Efforts to peel away a significant faction of the Liberal Party have become increasingly visible. PNL MEP Rareș Bogdan said that around 25–28 Liberal MPs were ready to support Niculescu’s government despite the party’s official position. Bogdan also said he would be willing to join Niculescu’s team, while PNL MP Alina Gorghiu has been mentioned as a possible justice minister. These manoeuvres seem to echo a recurring PSD strategy, reportedly pursued with the support of president Nicușor Dan, aimed at weakening the reformist faction within the PNL in favour of the more opportunistic and collaborative faction that controlled the party before the 2024 elections. At a meeting on October 12, the PSD decided to condition its participation in the government on Niculescu accepting its proposed governing strategy and the Liberals joining the coalition. Grindeanu reiterated that his party would prefer to hold the prime minister’s office itself, while also saying that the PSD was ready for early elections. The Liberals remain open to initially voting to invest Niculescu’s government. PNL Senate leader Mircea Abrudean said the party would decide whether to support the cabinet once it had received the government programme and list of ministers. “We are waiting for the government programme and the cabinet list to make a decision within the statutory forums of the PNL. At this moment, we express our openness to giving a vote of support, of investiture, for the Luca Niculescu government,” he said. Abrudean added that the PNL would not support the government if a faction of the party decided to join the cabinet. The PNL itself would not participate in the Government, he stressed. USR suggested a centre-right cabinet headed by Niculescu. Save Romania Union (USR) president Dominic Fritz said, after meeting the prime minister-designate, that a government formed by the PNL, USR and the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR) was the solution to the political deadlock. He added that, if such a government failed to secure a majority, early elections would be the healthiest solution for the country and the most honest option for citizens. “A PNL-USR-UDMR government with him [Luca Niculescu] as prime minister is certainly something we would look at with great openness. We have seen that Sorin Grindeanu is also open to such an option, and this may be the unblocking we need,” Fritz said.

data.title: InterCapital lists Polish equities ETF on Bucharest Stock Exchange
data.description: The ETF, traded under the ticker ICWIGETF, initially has less than RON 200,000 worth of units listed on the BVB. Additional units will be issued as demand grows. The fund was launched in May on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, where its assets reached EUR 13 mln. “It’s relatively new,” Đivo Pulitika, portfolio manager at InterCapital Asset Management, told Profit.ro , explaining that the firm had previously avoided promoting investments in Poland because measures introduced by the country’s political leadership towards the end of the previous decade had slowed the development of its capital market. The listing gives Romanian investors access to Poland, an economy worth around EUR 1 trillion, and its stock market, where more than 750 companies are listed. The Warsaw Stock Exchange has an aggregate market capitalisation exceeding EUR 600 billion and an average daily trading value of around EUR 600 million, according to the figures cited in the report.

data.title: Romania’s trade gap narrows by 4.5% y/y to 8.4% of GDP in 12 months to August
data.description: Trade flows gained momentum partly due to base effects, with exports increasing by 11.6% y/y to EUR 7.55 billion and imports by 13.7% to EUR 10.69 billion. However, over the 12 months to August, the rolling trade deficit narrowed by 4.5% y/y to EUR 33.17 billion. The deficit-to-GDP ratio also improved, falling to an estimated 8.4% over the 12 months to August, from 9.4% a year earlier. The nominal trade deficit offers no clear indication of a sustained improvement, having widened again in recent months amid high energy prices. By contrast, the deficit-to-GDP ratio has stabilised at around 8.4% since March. Slight currency depreciation, subdued private consumption and weak economic activity could further improve the ratio. However, progress towards a stronger external balance is likely to remain limited without structural changes in the composition of economic activity.

data.title: Romania’s debt-to-GDP ratio drops below 60% after GDP revision
data.description: The debt-to-GDP ratio reached 59.8%, up from 58.9% at the end of 2025, based on Romania Insider calculations using revised GDP figures. The dynamics of public debt and the indebtedness ratio during the first seven months of 2026 reveal three notable aspects: the entire revised debt-to-GDP trajectory is now below the 60% threshold; the ratio increased by only 0.9 percentage points during the period; and the entire increase in public debt was generated by debt denominated in foreign currency, while debt denominated in local currency remained broadly unchanged. The statistics office revised upwards 2024–2026 GDP, particularly in nominal terms. On October 9, the statistics office announced revised Q2 GDP figures, as well as revised semi-permanent figures for 2025 and permanent figures for 2024. The revisions to real GDP growth were modest: from 0.7% to 0.8% for 2024, from 0.9% to 1.1% for 2025, and from -0.7% to -0.6% for H1 2026. However, GDP deflators were also revised upwards, resulting in increases in nominal GDP of 0.4% for 2024, 0.7% for 2025 and 1.3% for H1 2026. GDP revision lowers debt-to-GDP ratios by around 0.4 percentage points. Following the revision, the debt-to-GDP ratio at the end of 2025 fell from 59.3% to 58.9%. More importantly, the ratio at the end of March dropped from 60.1% - the first time it had exceeded the 60% threshold - to 59.7%. The ratio at the end of July also fell, from 60.4% to 59.8%, and could decrease further once Q3 GDP data are released. The downward revisions are not large enough to alter the underlying macroeconomic picture, but the 60% threshold has practical implications. Exceeding it triggers measures the government must undertake, including a debt-reduction plan to be implemented from the semester following the one in which the threshold was breached. The debt-to-GDP ratio has risen relatively moderately so far this year. The 0.9 percentage-point increase between the end of 2025 and the end of July compares with a rise of 4.1 percentage points in 2025 and almost 6 percentage points in 2024. The lower rise in public debt was partly due to a narrower public deficit (financing needs). The government recorded a smaller budget deficit in the first part of this year, at 2.0% of GDP against 3.6% in the same period of 2025. In addition, the Treasury has postponed foreign-currency bond issues until a full government is appointed, a milestone that has yet to be reached. Foreign-currency debt accounts for the entire increase in public debt. Public debt denominated in local currency, which accounted for 44% of the total at the end of July, stood at RON 536 billion, up just 0.03% from the end of 2025. By contrast, debt denominated in foreign currency, predominantly euros, increased by 11.2% year-to-date when measured in local currency, or RON 67.5 billion. Expressed in euros, the increase was 8.1%, equivalent to EUR 9.5 billion, although not all the debt is denominated in euros. This increase represents the funds raised by the Government in foreign currency, alongside the RON 173 million raised through debt denominated in local currency. Short-term public debt has declined but remains historically elevated. After standing at around RON 80 billion at the ends of 2024 and 2025 amid tight budget execution, short-term public debt fell to RON 60 billion at the end of July. This remains above the RON 50 billion recorded at the end of 2023, RON 40 billion at the end of 2022, and RON 30 billion at the end of 2021.

data.title: One United Properties buys EUR 10 mln Bucharest site for mixed-use tower
data.description: Romanian real estate developer One United Properties announced that it acquired a 5,755 sqm plot on the Barbu Văcărescu Street in Bucharest for EUR 10 million. The company plans to build a residential-led mixed-use tower with an estimated gross development value of EUR 130 million. According to the preliminary concept, the building will have four underground levels, a ground floor, and 25 upper floors. Its above-ground gross built area is expected to reach approximately 25,900 sqm. The lower levels will include retail and office space, while the project will also provide around 2,000 sqm of green space. At more than 100 metres, it would become one of Romania’s tallest residential buildings. One United Properties plans to hold an international architecture competition to select the tower’s design. “We chose this site for its location and for the way it complements our investments in Floreasca-Barbu Văcărescu,” said Andrei Diaconescu, co-founder and co-CEO of One United Properties. “We will be looking for a design that makes the most of the site’s position and views, paying as much attention to the tower’s silhouette as to the way the building opens up to the street.” The company has completed developments worth approximately EUR 536 million in the Floreasca-Barbu Văcărescu area. Projects currently under construction there, including One Floreasca Sunset, One Peninsula, and One Floreasca Club, have a combined estimated value of EUR 360 million. The newly acquired property is located near One Gallery, the former Ford Hall restored by the developer, and has access to Bucharest’s northern business district, the A3 motorway, and the tram line connecting the area to Băneasa Airport and Bucur Obor. One United Properties, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange under the ticker ONE, develops residential, office and mixed-use projects, with a focus on urban regeneration in Bucharest.

data.title: Romanian film review: BIEFF and The Stranger
data.description: Vanishing futures: this was the motto of the Bucharest International Experimental Film Festival (BIEFF) and its fantastic selection proposed new ways to imagine a future that seems now more blurred than ever. The festival wrapped on 30 September and it visited cinema Studio in Timișoara this past weekend. I could not have picked one screening to recommend over another (yes, that good!), but in the interest of keeping this column compact, I will pick a few titles that stayed with me. The winner of the national short film competition, Andreea Chiper’s Three Bedtime Stories/ Trei povești de noapte bună listens to three women talk about their lives and deceased husbands; playful, moving, perceptive. It was also the most wholesome common experience; there was so much laughter in the audience. The short is also available for free in Cinepub as well, and you can watch it here (in Romanian only): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BLaWa1MMmc4&t=378s Alma Buhagiar’s In My Dreams, or in Ours (winner of Best Visual Concept) is a rapturous tale of eroticism and looking. Another beauty is Cosmin Nicolae’s Cherry Master , a story of loneliness in an eerie Bucharest by night. This was a great edition for visually striking colours and textures: I also loved Patri Preda and Alina Brăcaci’s Uprooting/ Dezrădăcinare , in which a daughter reflects on her her relationship with her mother. And then there is the avantgarde classics programme, amazing on a big screen, from the famous, multi-quoted Meshes of the Afternoon (Maya Deren, 1943) and La Jetée (Chris Marker, 1962, still one of the most ingenious, mind-boggling films ever made) to Artavazd Peleshian’s lyrical essay on the life of Armenian shepherds The Seasons (1975), or Peter Tscherkassky’ brain and eyeball-melting horror metafiction Outer Space (1999). https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AALcMGHg9po Fresh in cinemas across the country and also in Timișoara (to stay here a bit longer) is François Ozon’s The Stranger/ L’ Étranger . Based on Albert Camus’s eponymous novel, its protagonist is Meursault, a taciturn, apathetic young clerk working in French-colonised Algiers who kills an Arab man and endures the following events with barely any reaction. Meursault is such an impenetrable, passive character (played by Benjamin Voisin’s with precise, aloof elegance) that the second part of the film can be maddeningly frustrating until it all explodes in a perfectly staged release, a confrontation between Mersault and a chaplain who visits him in prison (perennial scene-stealer Swann Arlaud). The first part of the film, by contrast, is hypnotic and sensual. Meursault may be an enigma, but a seductive one, and Ozon tackles questions of morality, love, colonialism with (maybe too much) restraint but with his usual refinement. Easily the most beautiful film I’ve seen this year. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eh8tyaO6S3g

data.title: Four in ten Romanians unable to face unexpected expenses, Eurostat says
data.description: Four in ten Romanians (37.8%) cannot afford an unexpected financial expense, according to Eurostat data published on Sunday, October 11, for the year 2025. Romania had the fifth-highest share of citizens who could not face unexpected expenses if necessary in the EU, after Greece (50.5%), Latvia (43.7%), Bulgaria (42.4%) and Lithuania (41.1% – provisional data). In 2019, 44% of Romania’s population was in this situation, while in 2024, Eurostat placed Romania among the countries where at least 40% of the population was affected, alongside Bulgaria, Latvia, Greece and Lithuania. At the European level, the long-term trend is one of improvement: from a peak of 40% in 2012, following the financial crisis, the share fell to 30.8% in 2019, rose to 32.5% during the pandemic, and reached 30.0% in 2024. Meanwhile, the EU average stood at 29.2% in 2025. Moreover, according to Eurostat, only 0.4% of Romanians are behind on mortgage or rent payments, the lowest level in the EU. That is because only 1.5% of Romania’s population has a mortgage, compared with 58.1% in the Netherlands. However, when utility bills and installment payments for purchases are also included, 15.3% of Romanians are late with payments, compared with the EU average of 9.2%.

At the European level, the long-term trend is one of improvement: from a peak of 40% in 2012, following the financial crisis, the share fell to 30.8% in 2019, rose to 32.5% during the pandemic, and reached 30.0% in 2024. Meanwhile, the EU average stood at 29.2% in 2025. Moreover, according to Eurostat, only 0.4% of Romanians are behind on mortgage or rent payments, the lowest level in the EU. That is because only 1.5% of Romania’s population has a mortgage, compared with 58.1% in the Netherlands. However, when utility bills and installment payments for purchases are also included, 15.3% of Romanians are late with payments, compared with the EU average of 9.2%.

data.title: Dacia Foundation for Romania pledges EUR 1 mln grant to support social mobility
data.description: Dacia Foundation for Romania (FDpR), an autonomous non-profit organization sponsored by carmaker Dacia, announced the winners of the second edition of the “Mobilitatea contează” (“Mobility Matters”) grant program, which had a budget of up to EUR 1 million for projects that facilitate access to education, the labor market, and culture. In total, 28 non-governmental organizations received funding, among which 10 NGOs through the Continuity track, dedicated to strengthening projects supported in the first edition, and 18 through the Open Call track. “For us, mobility means having the opportunity to get from one place to another, which we call physical mobility, but also having access to education, a career path, and culture, and ultimately having the chance to build a better life, that is, social mobility,” said Adrian Curaj, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dacia Foundation for Romania. In the first year of the “Mobilitatea contează” program, 35 funded organizations worked directly with 13,500 beneficiaries and tested solutions to remove a wide variety of barriers to social mobility. Dacia Foundation for Romania also conducted an analysis of social mobility from the perspective of civil society, with 30 of the 35 partner organizations participating in August–September. A total of 82.8% of the organizations surveyed identified family environment or community of origin among the main causes of the physical and social mobility barriers faced by their beneficiaries. Limited access to education and training, lack of financial resources, and discrimination or stigmatization were also identified as causes of barriers by 69% of NGOs. According to the data, the place and environment in which a person grows up can influence the resources available to them, the education they can access, the support network they can rely on, and, in turn, the opportunities they can take advantage of. Educational support and access to training represented the main need identified by 79.3% of NGOs, followed by the development of support networks and connections with the community (69%). The responses highlighted the need to complement education with career guidance, personal development, and independent living skills, so that the knowledge acquired translates into autonomy and concrete employment opportunities. A total of 75.9% of NGOs considered partnerships between organizations, companies, and public institutions to be among the interventions with the greatest impact on social mobility, while 72.4% identify the development of support networks and communities as a priority. The data show how important it is for the resources provided to an individual to be backed by a community that helps them make the most of opportunities. Beyond identifying barriers and needs in communities, the organizations were invited to describe the changes they observed as a result of the projects funded in the first edition. The responses converge around four areas: increased confidence and autonomy, educational and professional integration, reduced isolation, and the development of practical skills. This perspective is also reflected in the way Dacia Foundation for Romania designed the second edition of the program, allocating a budget of up to EUR 1 million to projects that remove barriers to access to education, the labor market, and culture. In the 2026–2027 edition, 28 NGOs will receive funding. Ten organizations receive funding through the Continuity track, with a budget of up to EUR 300,000, to develop and expand interventions that demonstrated results in the first edition. Another 18 organizations were selected through the Open Call, with a budget of up to EUR 700,000, bringing new solutions and interventions into the program. Over the next 12 months, the projects will reach more than 15,000 beneficiaries in communities across the country, helping eliminate concrete physical and social mobility barriers and facilitating access to education, the labor market, and culture.

data.title: Healthcare in 2027: European investment, predictable financing, modernisation and resilience for a sustainable system
data.description: From healthcare financing in 2027 and hospital modernisation to access to medicines and crisis preparedness, the transformation of the healthcare system highlights the need for predictable resources, more effective services and better coordination between institutions. For patients, the stakes are tangible: more accessible care, timely access to treatment and continuity of healthcare services when they need them most. These topics were discussed at the National Public Health Conference #UndeDoare , organized by BUCHAREST CENTER FOR ECONOMY & SOCIETY (CES Bucharest). The event brought together representatives of national and European authorities, doctors, experts, industry representatives and patient organizations to discuss sustainable financing, the role of technology in improving system performance, the balance between innovation and the availability of medicines, and the capacity to deliver an integrated emergency response. At least EUR 20 billion for healthcare proposed for the next EU budget Victor Negrescu, Vice-President of the European Parliament, presented his proposals to include healthcare among the priorities of the European Union's next budget for 2028 to 2034. "In my capacity as rapporteur in the European Parliament's Committee on Public Health, I have proposed a dedicated healthcare chapter in the future national and regional partnership plans and called for a minimum allocation of EUR 20 billion for investment in healthcare." said Victor Negrescu. The MEP also advocated retaining the EU4Health programme and a dedicated European instrument for healthcare , as the European Commission's proposal no longer includes the programme as a standalone instrument. He also called for medical research, innovation and the development of new treatments and technologies to be funded through the future European Competitiveness Fund. Healthcare system resilience: institutional cooperation and secure digital infrastructure Lucian Fatu, State Secretary, President of the Euro-Atlantic Resilience Centre (E-ARC), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE), highlighted the role of interinstitutional and civil-military cooperation in ensuring continuity of healthcare services during crises. "Representatives involved in the supply of blood, plasma and derived medicines identified, first and foremost, the need for national planning that can simultaneously provide care for those injured in a kinetic conflict and ensure continuity of care for transfusion-dependent patients, with resources prioritized according to clear medical criteria. Civil-military planning, long-term blood storage and a steady blood supply are also needed." said Lucian Fatu. He referred to the exercise scheduled for 18 and 19 November at the Dr. Constantin Papilian Military Emergency Clinical Hospital in Cluj, designed to test medical evacuation and the management of mass-casualty incidents amid hybrid attacks and disruptions to critical infrastructure . Continuity of healthcare services also depends on reliable digital infrastructure and secure communications, emphasized Major General Eng. Gabriel David, First Deputy Director, Special Telecommunications Service (STS). "The Special Telecommunications Service provides the public healthcare sector with everything from applications and hosting to infrastructure, communications and networks that interconnect medical institutions. Every service must be available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, because any interruption can have consequences, sometimes serious ones. Security is equally important, because the exposure of patient data would be extremely serious. This year, we completed the construction of four new data centres, which can also be made available to the healthcare sector." said Major General Eng. Gabriel David, First Deputy Director, Special Telecommunications Service. Hospital investment must support healthcare services that remain operational over the long term Vlad Mixich, Health Policy Expert and Team Leader, European Investment Bank (EIB), highlighted the need for a long-term approach to investment in healthcare infrastructure that considers both the financing required to build or modernize hospitals and the resources needed to operate them. "Any major investment in Romania's healthcare system must demonstrate the sustainability of human resources over the medium and long term. There is little point in building new hospitals or renovating existing ones if we do not have the doctors and nurses, with the required specialisations and in sufficient numbers, to operate a hospital according to the standards of 21st-century medicine." said Vlad Mixich, Health Policy Expert and Team Leader at the European Investment Bank. From treating disease to prevention and assessing patient outcomes Representatives of the healthcare professions also highlighted the importance of prevention and a patient-centred approach to care. Prof. Valeriu Gheorghita, MD, PhD, Director General, Prof. Dr. Agrippa Ionescu Emergency Clinical Hospital, and Member of the Infectious Diseases Commission of the Romanian College of Physicians, advocated a shift from financing healthcare services based on their volume to models that take patient outcomes into account. "I believe that improving the efficiency of the healthcare system will only be possible when outcomes are linked to financing. In other words, when we move from what is known as fee-for-service, meaning payment based on the number of services provided regardless of their results, to what is known as value-based care, where the outcomes achieved through the services we provide also matter. We do not need to invent something that works here in Romania; we simply need to look at what others have done and try to adapt it to our country's circumstances." said Valeriu Gheorghita. Assoc. Prof. Adrian Pana, MD, PhD, Director, National Centre for Public Health Statistics, National Institute of Public Health (INSP), drew attention to the importance of primary healthcare and investment in public health. "Hospital care and medicines account for 80% of our current spending. Changing this balance requires a shared understanding; the National Health Insurance House cannot do it alone. Better data, a stronger focus on public health and properly delivered basic services free up funding for more efficient hospitals." said Adrian Pana. Access to patient data would also enable pharmacists to contribute more to treatment safety. Anca Crupariu, Pharmacist and Spokesperson for the Romanian College of Pharmacists, explained: "Digitalisation would be a breath of fresh air for pharmacies in Romania. If the electronic health record were integrated into the platform, pharmacists could access patients' medical histories." said Anca Crupariu. The need for greater investment in prevention is also reflected in children's oral health: according to data presented by Dr. Florin Dan Cezar Lazarescu, President of the Romanian Dental Council, 66% of children have dental caries, and only one in two brushes their teeth twice a day . "Given budgetary constraints, we consider investment in prevention a priority. A gradual shift from reimbursing curative treatments towards preventive treatments could bring us long-term benefits." said Florin Dan Cezar Lazarescu. The National Public Health Conference #UndeDoare was organized by BUCHAREST CENTER FOR ECONOMY & SOCIETY (CES Bucharest), in partnership with the Carol I Central University Library, with the support of MSD, Medtronic, Reteaua de Sanatate REGINA MARIA and Uniunea Nationala a Societatilor de Asigurare si Reasigurare din Romania (UNSAR).

data.title: Romania indicts 16 Russians over forged citizenship certificates and identity documents
data.description: The General Prosecutor’s Office announced on Monday, October 12, that it indicted 16 Russians for using forged citizenship certificates to obtain Romanian identity documents. The defendants, citizens of the Russian Federation, repeatedly used false citizenship certificates that falsely attested to their status as Romanian citizens to obtain Romanian identity documents, according to the authorities. Specifically, between February and July 2024, the defendants used citizenship certificates purportedly issued by the Consulate General of Romania in St. Petersburg, the Embassy of Romania in Baku, the Embassy of Romania in the Republic of Moldova, and the Consulate General of Romania in Chișinău. “These falsely attested that they had acquired Romanian citizenship, and on their basis, the defendants obtained the transcription of their birth certificates in the National Register of Persons, the assignment of Romanian personal identification numbers, and the issuance of Romanian birth certificates by the Local Council of District 6,” prosecutors said, cited by Agerpres . Subsequently, they obtained identity cards issued by the Câmpulung Moldovenesc Local Community Public Service for Personal Records. Based on those identity cards, they obtained simple electronic passports issued by the Suceava Community Public Service for Passports. The money obtained by the individuals who fictitiously provided the defendants with registered addresses is to be confiscated. The prosecutor in charge of the case also asked the court to annul the forged citizenship certificates, the entries in the civil status registers concerning the defendants’ births and their birth and marriage records, the birth certificates, as well as the subsequent documents obtained based on the forged citizenship certificates, namely the identity cards and passports. Overall, following checks carried out by police at the properties where the defendants and other foreign citizens born in the former Soviet space had established their residences, the General Directorate for Persons Records had to cancel 1,702 identity cards because the registered residences were fictitious. The indictment was sent to the Câmpulung Moldovenesc Court, the court competent to hear the case at first instance. In connection with this case, six plea agreements had previously been concluded, involving the same legal classification and the same pattern of facts.

data.title: Romanian-founded VoicePatrol raises USD 3.4 million for international expansion, technology development
data.description: VoicePatrol, a startup that developed an AI-powered voice moderation technology enabling gaming studios to detect and address extreme voice-chat toxicity, has raised USD 3.4 million in an investment led by GapMinder, a venture capital firm investing in technology startups from Romania and Eastern Europe. The VC is investing alongside Impact Ventures, Ollin Ventures, and The Build Fund. The investment will support VoicePatrol’s global expansion and the development of its AI-powered voice moderation technology. VoicePatrol’s approach starts by showing gaming studios the true scale of severe toxicity in their voice chat. Through a free two-week audit based on live monitoring and flagging of public lobbies, the company reveals the gap between the incidents studios already know about and those that go undetected.  VoicePatrol cuts severe toxicity by 55%-75% within three weeks, while reducing moderation costs by 30%-70% and expanding coverage to 100% of public lobbies, it said. The company, co-founded by Matei Trebien and Cătălin Cășuneanu , works with gaming businesses ranging from independent studios to AAA developers, across PC, console, and VR platforms. “Gaming is a USD 213.9 billion global industry, and as multiplayer experiences continue to scale, player safety is becoming a critical challenge for game developers and platforms. VoicePatrol is solving this problem at the infrastructure level, using AI to detect extreme toxicity in real time and take action within 5 seconds. We invested because Matei and the VoicePatrol team have built a technology that addresses a real pain point at massive scale. And we believe live voice moderation will become an essential part of the multiplayer gaming stack,” Robert Herscovici, Investment Director at GapMinder VC, said. “I was a teenager who used bad language in video games too. Because, come on, it’s fun. But there’s a difference between that and being genuinely insufferable. Or an actual predator. Studios hire us to find those people. We have three rules. First, we monitor public lobbies only. Second, there are no automatic kicks or bans; those decisions should be made manually after human review. Third, audio is deleted after processing, except in the most severe cases, where it can be retained as evidence,” Matei Trebien, CEO and Co-Founder of VoicePatrol, explains. “The machine-learning challenge is really twofold. We need to leave normal banter and competitive trash talk alone, and that requires a deep understanding of gaming context, not just simple keyword matching. Then we need to run everything fast and cheaply on our own AWS infrastructure, without third-party API calls adding latency and cost. If we do this well, games simply become more fun,” he added. GapMinder Ventures is a venture capital firm that invests in technology startups created in Romania and Eastern Europe that are in the seed or late seed phase and are rapidly expanding internationally. With the first fund having a total capitalization of EUR 50 million, GapMinder has invested in: Druid.AI, FintechOS, Veridion, Deepstash, Siena.Cx, TypingDNA, Medicai, Cyscale, SmartDreamers, Machinations, Frisbo, and Innoship.io. GapMinder Fund II was launched in 2024 with a target capital of EUR 80 million. The EIF supported GapMinder Fund II through two initiatives: the European Union's InvestEU program and the Recovery Fund of Funds—part of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, co-financed by the EU through Next GenerationEU. GapMinder Fund II is also supported by the EBRD and several institutional and private investors.

data.title: Whitaker Says ‘No Change’ to Arms Flows to Kyiv via PURL
data.description: On Monday, US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker said that he knew of no change to Washington’s weapon policies to Ukraine via NATO, saying he does not wish to comment on “unconfirmed reports.” Whitaker also acknowledged Kyiv’s air defense shortage but said he viewed it as a “short-term challenge,” with “a lot of companies” working on alternatives to fill the gap.

data.title: IMF Warns Europe’s Growth Will Slow as Russia’s War, Middle East Crisis Drive Up Energy Costs
data.description: The International Monetary Fund forecasts eurozone growth of just 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027, warning that Russia’s war against Ukraine and the Middle East conflict are driving up energy costs and prolonging inflation. At its World Economic Outlook briefing, IMF officials also warned of risks to Gulf economies and highlighted the growing dependence of global trade on artificial intelligence.

data.title: ‘They Agreed Because I Said They Agreed’ – Trump Insists Ukraine, Russia Accepted Energy Ceasefire Despite Denials
data.description: US President Donald Trump insisted Monday, Oct. 12, that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire because he told them to, despite neither government confirming such a deal. Trump dismissed questions about continued Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and claimed Putin was more eager to reach a peace agreement than Zelensky. His remarks came amid growing controversy over Washington’s decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel.

data.title: Belgium, Germany, Italy, Seek ‘Emergency Brake’ on New EU Laws
data.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever, urged an “emergency brake” allowing EU capitals to stop new legislation that the countries may perceive as burdensome. Their letter to European Council President António Costa, as seen by Politico, comes ahead of an Oct. 15–16 EU summit in Brussels, where energy prices, competitiveness and further support for Ukraine will be discussed.

data.title: Russia Strikes Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles After Deadly Drone Attack Kills 2
data.description: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late Monday, Oct. 12, hours after a drone struck a residential high-rise, killing two people. Ukraine’s Air Force reported that approximately six ballistic missiles targeted several districts at around 10:10 p.m., with no advance warning of their launch. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported strikes on transport infrastructure and a four-story warehouse.

data.title: EU States Unanimously Agree to Open 2 New Accession Clusters for Ukraine
data.description: According to Ireland’s Minister of State for European Affairs and Defense, the EU member states have unanimously agreed to open accession Clusters 2 and 3 – internal market and competitiveness and inclusive growth – for Ukraine and Moldova. The decision came hours after Ukraine adopted a minority education law that Hungary had demanded in exchange for lifting its veto on the EU bid.

data.title: Japan Signs Contract for Ukraine's SkyFall Interceptor Drones
data.description: Japan’s Defense Ministry signed a contract to buy interceptor drones from Ukraine’s SkyFall and is working on early delivery, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi told reporters. He pointed to Ukraine’s rapid feedback cycle, in which upgraded drones appear every 2-3 weeks, as a lesson for Japan’s defense industry. Tokyo is not considering weapons transfers to Ukraine under its Self-Defense Forces law.

data.title: Trump Defends Russia Diesel Deal as Zelensky Says Moscow Ignores Truce
data.description: US President Donald Trump has defended his abrupt diesel deal with Russia despite criticism from Republican and Democratic senators and European allies. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine held off striking Russian energy sites after Trump announced a truce, but that Russia showed no sign of complying and continued striking Ukraine nationwide.

data.title: UK’s Burnham Says Russia Interfered in 2016 Brexit Vote, Warns of Similar Activity in France, Germany
data.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham claimed Russia had interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum, marking the first such statement by a sitting British leader. Although he did not provide specific details, he warned of similar Russian interference activity in France and Germany. Meanwhile, a pro-Brexit group accused him of undermining the vote’s legitimacy.

data.title: Ukraine Adapts Air Defense to Counter Faster Russian Jet Drones
data.description: Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense says Russia is deploying small groups of jet-powered drones across different regions, prompting Kyiv to develop new ways to intercept them. data.title: ‘Let’s Sign a Diesel Deal’: Zelensky Challenges Trump
data.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed that Donald Trump sign a “diesel deal” with Ukraine, arguing that Russian supplies are too small to influence global prices. Kyiv would suspend attacks on Russian oil infrastructure in exchange for guaranteed protection of Ukraine’s electricity system. Zelensky also warned that Russia’s Black Sea blockade could trigger food shortages in Africa, Asia and the Middle East.

data.title: Kremlin Offers Just 1 Day Ceasefire in Response to Kyiv’s 60-Day Ceasefire Proposal for Elections
data.description: As Kyiv calls for a 60-day ceasefire to hold elections following Trump’s call for one in Ukraine, the Kremlin poured cold water on the idea on Monday, claiming Kyiv could use the time to regroup and offering only a one-day ceasefire on the proposed election day itself. Despite the calls, many hurdles remain to holding a truly representative election during wartime.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE
PERSISTENTE. BÔ DISSAL I NA BIN FASSI PASSSAÇÃO LI. tUDO PUBLICAÇÕES KU I FASSI
I NA RESP+UNDI PAREL. NIN IKANA SEDU DIDIA. NONA VINGAL MANERA KU NÓ PUDI. JÁ
TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU
AGRESSÃO E NESTE MOMENTO ESTÁ EM QUELUZ EM PORTUGAL. FILHO DA PUTA. MENTIROSO
COMO OS TEUS PATRÕES OS SUJOS JOMAV E BRAIMA CAMARÁ. MARCOS GALINA, BU NA
ARREPENDI. PERA BU DJUBI. ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E
COMPRAS?! VAMOS PROVAR DEPOIS. FIDJU DI BALETA Olá a todos, ainda bem que descobriram
que o Pirata informático- hackec é o Marcos Galina Barbosa, Eng. Informático.
Tentei várias vezes avisar o Ticha Aly Silva mas ele não respondeu e nem deu
importância julgo eu. No tempo da campanha para a liderança do Paigc, este
indivíduo era um fervoroso apoiante do Bá Quecuto no Facebook e a técnica que
usava era o envio de Phishing aos apoiantes do Dsp, recolhia informações
pessoais das pessoas que posteriormente eram expostas no Blog do Doka. Tentou
comigo mas não resultou. Tenham cuidado com este sujeito que está nas mãos de
B. Camara. Outra coisa, gostaria de conhecer a vossa página no Fecebook. Estamos Juntos. AC Nota GP: Até jovens inocentes,
Lesmes, Masta Tito e demais outros, os tais vendidos e comprados foram as tuas
vítimas. teu filho da puta que o bandido de Baciro Djá trouxe para Bissau para funções no aparelho de Estado e dizes que outros recebem favores.
Desde quando é que és mais honesto ou
mais competentes que os outros? Pagas e até pode ser com a tua vida para
perceberes as irresponsabilidades
dos teus actos. Publicada por O

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP não respeita os antigos combatentes e sempre usou e abusou desses camaradas. Prova disso é que continuou a governar mesmo já com Carlos Correia como primeiro ministro. Usou até o cadáver de Carmem Perreira para promover sua imagem, pois é sabido que a malograda como sendo antigo combatente e membro do PAIGC o corpo só deveria passar por ANP e sede do partido e nunca na Primatura como aconteceu, e por cima de tudo com indivíduos alí barricados por vontade própria vandalizando instituição do estado o que demonstra uma clara promoção ao anarquismo. Não respeitou nem o Pai da Nação(ALC), nem o PR quanto mais o formalismo de um estado de direito democrático, prova disso mais uma vez, o ganancioso após o PR ter depositado coroas de flores no túmulo de ALC no dia dos heróis nacionais, reuniu os seus "gangs" para o mesmo efeito, conseguiu até mobilizar um dos familiares do Pai da Nação para lhe acompanhar tudo isso para manipular e dividir os guineenses "guineenses ku udjus fitchadu" para os seus intereses obscuros.
data.description: António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: Kraka Poku Tori biedt Surinaamse muziektalenten kansen voor groei en ondernemerschap
data.description: De tweede editie van Kraka Poku Tori vindt op 16 en 17 oktober plaats. Het Conservatorium van Suriname zet met seminars, workshops en een showcase in op talentontwikkeling, ondernemerschap en meer economische kansen voor Surinaamse musici. The proposed powers emerged during deliberations on the Bill at a workshop involving the Ministry of Education and Training […] The post Sebenta bill proposes new regulatory powers over non-formal education appeared first on Independent News Eswatini .

data.title: Eswatini Railways demands crackdown on scrapyards
data.description: Mbabane- Eswatini Railways wants scrap yard owners closely monitored to stop the trade in suspected stolen railway materials, raising fresh concerns about the security of critical national infrastructure and the cost of vandalism to the country’s economy. The call was made on October 12,2026 during the launch of Railway Safety Week at The George Hotel […] The post Eswatini Railways demands crackdown on scrapyards appeared first on Independent News Eswatini .
